messages.subject: Re: SAS, mapreduce and logs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Arihant,

You can read sas7bdat files from disk using the R package sas7bdat: http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/packages/info/?sas7bdat . But first you'll need to copy the file from HDFS to your local environment. You can use the read.hdfs function in the rhdfs package https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rhdfs to do that, but you'll need enough local disk space to hold it, and enough time to wait for it to copy over the network. Since the file is in Hadoop, this may not be easy.

A better solution is to leave the file in Hadoop and analyze it there. If it were a plaintext file you could possibly do something with rmr2 https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2, but that's not what you have. Revolution R Enterprise does have the capability to process and analyze SAS files in Hadoop, but this is a commercial product. (See: http://www.revolutionanalytics.com/revolution-r-enterprise )

As for the "complete log", in R the transcript of your interactive session serves as the log file.

Hope this helps,
# David Smith

messages.subject: Re: RSiteSearch doesn't open web browser. (RRO 3.2.0)
messages.body_plain:
Glad to hear that switching to R 3.2.1 made things work. This problem probably has to do with your web browser settings. The RSiteSearch() function will try to contact the URL 'http://search.r.-project.org' and will then try to open information on the term or expression
you searched on in an available web browser. This function will not work on a server machine that does not have a web browser.

You can set the R environment variable 'R_BROWSER' to tell R specifically what browser to use and this will be used by RSiteSearch(). You can set this in the file 'C:\Program Files\RRO\R-3.2.0\etc\Rprofile.site'
on Windows or in your user-specific .Rprofile file.

Here is an example:
R_BROWSER=${R_BROWSER-‘C:\Documents and Settings\abc\Local Settings\Application Data\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe'}

Stephen Weller

I am making a guess here: it seems you are using RStudio Server as opposed to RStudio Desktop.

RStudio Server will only recognize a single installation of R. I am guessing that you installed R before installing RRO, and RStudio server is still pointing to R.

To fix this, you have two options:

1. Reconfigure RStudio Server (instructions at https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200552316-Configuring-the-Server)

2. Install and use RStudio desktop - this allows you easily select the version of R you want to use.

I hope this helps

Andrie

Hi Ronald,

On Windows, Revolution R Open 3.2.1 can work side-by-side with any other version of CRAN R, including past version of RRO. In order to continue working with a different version of R from a terminal window, you must specify the full path to the R executable you want to use.

After the installation of RRO 3.2.1, you can launch Rgui.exe to start interacting with R.

For example, if you installed Revolution R Open 8.0.0 and then upgraded to Revolution R Open 3.2.1, here is how you could work with them side-by-side:
Start RRO 3.2.1 by executing C:\Program Files\RRO\R-3.2.1\bin\x64\Rgui.exe if that is where you installed RRO 3.2.1.
Start RRO 8.0.0 by executing C:\Program Files\RRO\R-3.1.1\bin\x64\Rgui.exe if that is where you installed RRO 8.0.0.

Hope that helps!

.libPaths("C:\Users\testRuser\MyRLibrary")
